question: Check whether the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ are coplanar. Justify your conclusion.
explanation:
Step 1: Identification of relevant vectors
For the two lines,
$$\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_1=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k},$$
$$\vec{a}_2=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_2=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Vector joining points on the lines
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{j}.$$
Step 3: Coplanarity criterion
The lines are coplanar if
$$\left(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2\right)=0.$$
Step 4: Evaluation of the scalar triple product
$$\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2=-3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}.$$
Therefore,
$$\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right)\cdot\left(-3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\right)=-3+3=0.$$
Step 5: Final conclusion
Since the scalar triple product is zero, the given lines are coplanar.

options.A: The lines are coplanar because the scalar triple product is $0$.
options.B: The lines are non-coplanar because the direction vectors are not proportional.
options.C: The lines are parallel and therefore coplanar.
options.D: The lines are non-coplanar because the scalar triple product is $-3$.
